output_json.patch_notes: src/main/java/org/apache/commons/io/FilenameUtils.java: (1) added imports java.util.Arrays, java.util.List, java.util.regex.Matcher, java.util.regex.Pattern; (2) added constants EMPTY_STRING_ARRAY, IPV4_PATTERN, IPV4_MAX_OCTET_VALUE, IPV6_MAX_HEX_GROUPS, IPV6_MAX_HEX_DIGITS_PER_GROUP, MAX_UNSIGNED_SHORT, BASE_16, REG_NAME_PART_PATTERN; (3) in getPrefixLength(), the UNC/double-separator branch now computes hostnamePart = filename.substring(2, pos-1) and returns NOT_FOUND unless isValidHostName(hostnamePart) is true; (4) added private helper methods isValidHostName, isIPv4Address, isIPv6Address, isRFC3986HostName (ported from the upstream Apache Commons IO 2.7 fix for this class of bug). src/test/java/org/apache/commons/io/FilenameUtilsTestCase.java: added testNormalize_CVE_2021_29425_pathTraversal(), asserting normalize()/getPrefixLength() reject '//../foo', '\\..\foo', '//..\foo', and malformed-hostname UNC prefixes like '//-server/foo' and '//.server/foo'.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change is narrowly scoped to inputs with a leading double path separator (UNC-style paths) whose apparent host/share segment is not a syntactically valid RFC 3986 host name or IPv6 literal — such inputs now yield null from normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() and -1 from getPrefixLength() instead of a previously-unvalidated result. Legitimate UNC paths ('//server/share/...', numeric-IP hosts, etc.) are unaffected, confirmed by the full pre-existing FilenameUtilsTestCase suite (38/38 pass, including the '//server/...' cases already in the suite) and FileSystemUtilsTestCase (28/28 pass). A full `mvn test` run shows 4 pre-existing failures (FileFilterTestCase.testCanRead/testCanWrite, FileUtilsCleanDirectoryTestCase.testThrowsOnCannotDeleteFile/testThrowsOnNullList) that reproduce identically on the unpatched baseline (verified via git stash) — they stem from file-permission-enforcement tests running as root in the container, unrelated to this change.
output_json.summary:
Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in FilenameUtils.normalize()/getPrefixLength() (the same root cause as CVE-2021-29425). For UNC-style inputs beginning with a double separator (e.g. '//../foo', '\\..\foo'), getPrefixLength previously computed the prefix length purely from the position of the next separator, without validating that the intervening text was a plausible host/share name. That let a '..' segment be silently swallowed into the 'prefix' portion of the path, where it is never touched by doNormalize's '..'-collapsing logic — so normalize() returned the traversal sequence unchanged/mishandled instead of rejecting it, letting callers that trust normalize() to keep paths inside an allowed directory be bypassed. FileSystemUtils.performCommand/openUnixStat build OS commands from normalize()'d, attacker-influenced paths, so those call sites are covered too, but the fix is entirely in FilenameUtils at the trust boundary.

Fix (matches the upstream Apache Commons IO 2.7 fix for IO-556/IO-559): getPrefixLength() now extracts the candidate host/share substring between the leading '//' or '\\' and the following separator and validates it via isValidHostName() (RFC 3986 host name or IPv6 literal) before treating it as a legitimate prefix. If the substring isn't a valid host name (e.g. '..', '-server', '.server'), getPrefixLength returns NOT_FOUND (-1), which makes doNormalize() return null instead of an unsanitized/ambiguous path. This blocks the highlighted '//../foo' path plus same-class variants: backslash form ('\\..\foo'), mixed separators ('//..\foo'), and malformed host names in general (leading hyphen, leading dot, etc.), while preserving legitimate UNC paths like '//server/a/b' (existing test suite covers these and continues to pass).
